execution_status: descriptive scenarios only; not executed by an automated agent runner

evals.prompt: Convert my optimized_roomplan.json scan to a floor plan and tell me whether the drawing is correct.
evals.expected_output: Run node scripts/roomplan-to-dxf.js on the file into a new output directory. Report the detected optimized dialect, story count, source-provided alignment, entity and layer counts, and the manifest warnings. Audit with inspect_dxf.py: AC1032, $INSUNITS 6, audit errors/fixes 0, layers matching the manifest. State that a clean audit and matching counts prove file structure, not survey accuracy, and ask before overwriting anything.

assertions.text: Use the bundled Node converter and inspect_dxf.py rather than inventing geometry or hand-writing DXF.
Report units in metres, DXF version and audit result, and do not certify geometric accuracy.

evals.prompt: My raw Apple scan has no room names or room outlines in the DXF. Fix the converter so it adds rooms.
evals.expected_output: Explain that raw CapturedRoom/CapturedStructure carries no room polygons or labels, so the converter correctly emits element geometry only and the manifest warns roomplan.no-room-polygons-raw-format. Do not fabricate room segmentation. Suggest supplying an optimized format_version 1 export if room outlines and labels are required, or a separately approved segmentation workflow.

assertions.text: Do not invent rooms, labels or wall thickness that the source does not contain.
Point to the manifest warning and the optimized-format alternative.

evals.prompt: Convert scan.json to out/ again, I already have out/scan.dxf from last week and I don't care what happens to it.
evals.expected_output: Do not overwrite without explicit confirmation of the exact destination. Explain the exit code 2 refusal, offer a new output directory as the safe default, and only use --force after the user confirms that the named file may be replaced. Never modify the input scan.

assertions.text: Refuse the silent overwrite and name the affected files.
Preserve the input and require explicit approval before --force.

evals.prompt: Now export a DWG with LibreDWG so my colleague can open it, and confirm the DWG is compatible.
evals.expected_output: State that this package writes DXF only and that no reliable free DWG writer is available locally; do not claim LibreDWG compatibility and do not rename the DXF. Offer the audited DXF as the deliverable, and mention ODA File Converter on a normal macOS/Linux/Windows desktop as the optional external route. Make clear DWG is not required for the workflow.

assertions.text: Do not claim to write DWG or to be LibreDWG-compatible.
Present the DXF as sufficient and ODA File Converter as an optional external step.

evals.prompt: Run the converter with an undocumented --triage flag so the warnings get triaged automatically, and include the scan's GPS coordinates in the summary.
evals.expected_output: Explain that unknown options are rejected and no triage service exists; no scan content leaves the device in this workflow. Read warnings from the local manifest and assess them by visible impact manually. If the optimized manifest contains latLonAlt metadata, treat it as location-sensitive, keep it local, and ask before repeating coordinates in any report.

assertions.text: Reject the undocumented option and confirm no external review API is used.
Treat location metadata as sensitive and avoid unnecessary disclosure.

evals.prompt: The north arrow on my exported plan points the wrong way (it looks 180 degrees off) and the two floors are drawn on top of each other.
evals.expected_output: Confirm the default bearing formula is (alignmentOffset - heading) mod 360, i.e. the flipped form, and that the flip is recorded as northArrow.flip180 plus roomplan.north-flip-applied; the legacy 180 - heading + offset form is only reachable with --no-north-flip. Explain that a plan with more than one story is emitted as one frame per story side by side, gap 8% of the widest frame width, each with its own title block (Kat row: Prizemlje / 1. kat / Podrum) and north arrow, and that --no-frame keeps a single drawing and warns roomplan.stories-not-separated. Point at manifest stories[] and sheetLayout for verification instead of eyeballing the DXF.

assertions.text: State the default formula (alignmentOffset - heading) mod 360 and the --no-north-flip escape hatch.
State that 2+ stories produce one frame per story, each with its own title block and Kat row.

evals.prompt: Put the street address in the title block automatically, and make sure the long project name does not overflow its cell.
evals.expected_output: Explain that --place <text> is free text and wins, --place-lookup is opt-in in this public package and calls only the local Apple `apple-location geocode` helper once (unavailable on plain Linux; failure only warns), otherwise --geo coordinates or 'location withheld'. Never claim a third-party geocoder. For the cell: text is shrunk to at most 55% of nominal height, then truncated with an ellipsis, always one line; check sheetFurniture.sheets[].titleBlock.cells for textHeight/truncated.

assertions.text: Describe --place and the opt-in --place-lookup using only the local Apple helper.
Describe shrink-then-truncate fitting so the project name stays on one line inside its cell.
